events.title: THE NEW HOLDING IS PLACED UNDER A SINGLE ESTATE ADMINISTRATION
events.body: The enlarged holding receives its first unified administrative order when Valerius directs the stewards to treat the newly acquired 15 square miles as one contiguous private estate system with the principal estate at its center. The existing 9,600 acres are entered into a single working register alongside their inherited buildings, fields, storage sites, waterworks, cart approaches, and the seasonal labor obligations already included in the acquisition price. Separate field books are retained for accounting purposes, but the stewards now coordinate maintenance, crop planning, labor scheduling, and movement through one estate administration rather than through the former parcel divisions. Valerius's sister is given access to the commercial portion of these records through the Merchant Affairs Office so that production information can be matched to actual merchant demand without mixing civic and private authority. No additional land is purchased and no new labor population is assumed from the administrative consolidation. The practical change is that the estate now has one internal chain for managing the full 22.959375-square-mile holding, while ownership, labor agreements, and public legal responsibilities remain separately recorded.

The office selects saleable estate material, matches part of it with needed commercial inputs, and sends the appropriate portion to established artisans whose work increases the value of the finished goods before the shipment is consigned through the existing merchant network. The office now has a concrete working record showing how surplus and necessary inputs can move through the same network without creating an exclusive merchant privilege or pre-booking future receipts.

events.title: AN OLD PROPERTY CLAIM SURFACES AGAINST A DRAINAGE CORRIDOR ON THE NEW ESTATE
events.body: A former steward from one of the properties absorbed into the new holding unexpectedly produces a duplicate property memorandum asserting that a narrow drainage corridor crossing the enlarged estate should remain subject to a separate maintenance entitlement. The document is old enough to have survived outside the final package of deeds, and its sudden appearance forces the estate stewards to compare seals, boundary descriptions, and the final transfer records rather than simply discard the claim. The review shows that the memorandum describes a maintenance arrangement associated with the former parcel division, not a surviving ownership right, and the claimant's requested permanent control is therefore rejected. The stewards nevertheless preserve any lawful drainage access that neighboring fields already depended upon, preventing the dispute from becoming an arbitrary closure of an established watercourse. No acreage is removed from the 22.959375-square-mile holding, no payment is made on the unsupported claim, and no new encumbrance is recorded. The incident is significant because the enlarged estate now contains old property relationships that can resurface even after the purchase has been completed, giving the new holding an active legal-history thread rather than a perfectly clean administrative slate.

events.title: A WINTER OBSTRUCTION AT THE LAKE PORT FORCES A SUDDEN COMMERCIAL REROUTING
events.body: A sudden winter obstruction at the lake port interrupts the normal loading rhythm used by carriers serving the estate, leaving one scheduled commercial movement unable to use its accustomed loading point on the expected day. Valerius's sister responds through the Merchant Affairs Office by separating the cargo into what can safely remain at the port and what can be redirected through an established overland approach connected to the principal estate. The lake port remains an active component of the trade network after the interruption, but the office now has a documented contingency procedure for short winter disruptions.
